title: Vertical Bloch-line memory revived in stacked synthetic antiferromagnet films
idea: Revive Konishi's 1983 vertical Bloch-line memory: store bits as pairs of Bloch lines inside the domain walls of stripe domains in stacked perpendicular synthetic-antiferromagnet films, stepping them along the walls with in-plane pulse fields. The domain wall itself is the track, so no lithographic cell exists.
why: Density and capital intensity: bits at wall-internal scale (~10-20 nm) with tiers added by sputtering; a mask-light bulk working memory candidate.

title: Purely electronic Mott-avalanche switching in lacunar spinel cross-points
idea: Electric-field-driven Mott transition: GaV4S8-family lacunar spinel films switch by an electronic avalanche that collapses the Mott gap, with no ion motion, into a retained metallic filament. Cross-point tiers of these films aim at RRAM-like density without oxygen-vacancy wear.
why: Gives a non-volatile 4F2 stackable cell (fact 2) with ion-free switching for DRAM-class endurance; claim >1e12 cycles in principle. Room-temperature retention is the risk.

title: Magnesiothermic reduction turns oxide pillars into porous-silicon capacitor electrodes
idea: Pattern SiO2 storage-node pillars by e-beam or i-line litho, react them with Mg vapor at ~650 C (2Mg + SiO2 -> Si + 2MgO), strip MgO in dilute HCl, and keep the resulting doped mesoporous Si as an electrode with ~5-10x surface area, finished with ALD Al2O3/ZrO2 and TiN.
why: Multiplies capacitance per footprint at low aspect ratio (fact 1), so a 10:1 pillar could hold what a 60:1 pillar holds; needs only a furnace, wet bench and ALD.

title: Abandoned molybdenum gates revived as recoverable, US-sourced wordline metal
idea: Molybdenum gates were tried in early MOS and dropped for polysilicon because of oxidation and processing problems. Replace tungsten in buried and 3D wordlines with ALD Mo under a nitride cap that blocks oxidation, and design the stack so the Mo can be selectively leached and recovered at end of life.
why: Removes the tungsten chokepoint (China ~80%) using U.S.-mined Mo, with lower resistivity at thin dimensions and closed-loop metal recovery.

title: Sodium-potassium pump: a 2T cell whose own feedback stays charged
idea: Neurons hold resting potential with a continuous pump; add a second vertical transistor per cell whose gate is the storage node and which feeds a weak bias rail back into the node, sized so its subthreshold current at '1' exceeds the node's 125 C leakage while at '0' it stays below the leak to ground, making the cell quasi-static.
why: Refresh-free at 125 C with one extra transistor (far cheaper than 6T SRAM) and stackable in vertical tiers; removes refresh power and bank blocking for automotive/industrial memory.

title: Parking-garage helicoid tiers via rotating glancing-angle deposition
idea: Thread-rolling and helical-ramp analogy: deposit the tier stack as one continuous helicoid ramp around a central pillar by glancing-angle deposition while rotating and slowly tilting the wafer, so each tier is one turn of a ramp and all tiers are reachable from the ramp edge without a staircase etch.
why: Staircase area and its many litho-trim loops grow with tier count (facts 2, 4); a helical ramp turns tier access into one contact row. Glancing-angle deposition makes 10-100 nm helices today, but not yet device-grade films.

title: Magnify access gate length 10x using free vertical space
idea: Since 3D arrays have spare height, make the vertical gate-all-around access channel about 300 nm long with a 5 nm thin body, instead of a short planar or recessed channel. This suppresses short-channel and DIBL leakage paths that create the 13 fA tail.
why: Refresh: a tighter leakage tail could stretch retention about 10x (64 ms to about 640 ms), cutting refresh energy and bandwidth loss by about 90%.

title: Vertical NEMS relays as zero-leakage DRAM access switches
idea: [Box: MIM charge | electrostatic vertical nanorelay | charge-share SA | BEOL over CMOS | Si | sacrificial release of a ~10 nm air gap] A vertically actuated nanocantilever touches the storage-node contact only while the wordline pulls it in; through an air gap the off-state leakage is essentially zero, so the cell holds charge for hours.
why: Refresh (fact 3) and voltage floor (fact 10): no subthreshold leakage and abrupt switching; contact endurance (1e12+ cycles) is the main risk.

title: Zinc-oxide sacrificial release lets PDMS stamps transfer-print memory tiers
idea: Build thin-film memory tiles (oxide TFTs plus capacitors) on a ZnO sacrificial layer, undercut it in dilute acetic acid while tethers hold the tiles, pick them up with a PDMS stamp and print them onto logic or the previous tier, stacking only known-good tiles.
why: Known-good-tile stacking breaks the yield multiplication across tiers (fact 2) without wafer-scale bonders; micro-transfer printing needs only a stamp stage that universities have or can build.

title: Rotate alternate 3D tiers 90 degrees to split staircases
idea: In a lateral 3D DRAM stack, rotate every other tier's cell orientation 90 degrees so odd-tier bitlines run X and even-tier bitlines run Y. Odd tiers stair-step on the east/west edges and even tiers on north/south, so each staircase is half as tall, and vertically adjacent bitlines only cross at points instead of running parallel.
why: 3D blockers (fact 2): staircase footprint per edge halves (~20-30% array-efficiency gain at 64+ tiers) and inter-tier bitline coupling drops ~5-10x, allowing thinner tiers.

title: Mass-transfer printing of pre-tested micro-tiles replaces monolithic stacking
idea: Substitute TSV die stacks or monolithic tiers with microLED-style elastomer-stamp mass transfer: 60x60 um DRAM sub-array micro-tiles (array + local SAs, ~3 um thick, released by sacrificial undercut) are tested on the source wafer and printed layer by layer onto a logic host with planarized redistribution vias between layers.
why: Yield and data movement (facts 5-6): bad tiles discarded at 60 um granularity instead of whole dies; memory sits within um of compute; tool base already exists in microLED fabs.

title: Oxide-CMOS sense amplifiers distributed inside every tier
idea: Under 400 C, each tier carries its own tiny sense-amp strip of n-IGZO and p-SnO transistors deposited at 250 C, sensing short local bitlines. The bonded base logic only handles global I/O.
why: Fact 7 and 3D scaling: periphery stops growing with tier count; local sensing tolerates small Cs.

title: Maskless three-beam interference lithography for hexagonal cell arrays
idea: Limit: no photomask for the array. Expose the whole cell field with three-beam laser interference, which prints a perfect hexagonal pillar lattice in one shot. Periphery is defined separately by cheap i-line or ArF litho and stitched at mat edges.
why: Fact 4: replaces several EUV array layers with a tool costing about 1/50 as much, and hex packing gains about 15% over square.

title: Harvested server DRAM dies restacked with sidewall-metallized interconnect
idea: Combine e-waste recovery with 3D stacking: dies desoldered from retired US hyperscaler DIMMs are retested, thinned, given an RDL that routes pads to one edge, glued into 8-16-high cubes, and wired together by laser-patterned metal on the lapped cube sidewall (Irvine Sensors-style), assembled at US OSATs.
why: Raises usable supply with near-zero wafer capital or scarce materials: retired DDR4/DDR5 dies become dense CXL capacity cubes; no TSVs (fact 6).

title: Maskless interference lithography for the array, one trim mask
idea: Reverse which part needs a mask: pattern the periodic capacitor lattice with three-beam 193 nm interference (no reticle) at ~70 nm pitch, multiply hole density with block-copolymer DSA, and add one cheap DUV trim mask that blocks the lattice outside the arrays.
why: EUV dependence and capital (fact 4): removes an EUV layer from the 5-7 per wafer, cutting critical-layer cost by roughly 3-5x.

title: Unipolar VCMA-MTJ with thin-film diode enables stacked cross-point MRAM
idea: Voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy: precessional writes with timed unipolar voltage pulses flip perpendicular MTJs at fJ energy, so each cell needs only a one-way thin-film diode instead of a transistor. Unipolar operation lets 4F2 MRAM cross-point tiers be repeated in BEOL.
why: Brings non-volatile MRAM to 4F2 density in 3D (facts 2 and 4) at near-DRAM speed; claim fJ writes and ~4x density versus 1T1MTJ.

title: Edge-standing bookshelf die stacks replace TSV vertical stacking
idea: Substitute horizontal TSV stacking with dies standing on edge like books: each thinned 30 um DRAM die routes I/O along its face to fine-pitch edge pads (exposed by dicing through scribe Cu bars), and 32-64 dies are laminated and bonded edge-down onto the base logic die, with heat leaving through full die faces to a top cold plate.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6): no TSVs, so no 3x area per bit or via yield loss; ~1-2k edge pads per die at 10 um pitch supports HBM-class width.

title: Hexagonal close-packed vertical cells reach the 3.46F2 packing limit
idea: Use cylinder-forming block-copolymer self-assembly over a coarse ArF guide pattern to place vertical channels on a hexagonal lattice, routing wordlines and bitlines along two of its three 60-degree axes so each cell occupies 2*sqrt(3)*F^2 instead of 4F^2.
why: Geometry is a hard minimum: hexagonal packing (0.907) beats square (0.785), giving ~13% more bits per area at the same F, while polymer chain length rather than EUV sets the 20-30 nm pitch, removing several of the 5-7 EUV layers (fact 4).

title: Crystal-plane KOH trenches on (110) silicon replace plasma deep etch
idea: Substitute fluorocarbon/Bosch deep etching with crystallographic wet etching: on (110) Si, KOH/TMAH etches trenches bounded by vertical {111} planes at AR >100:1 with atomically smooth walls; a dedicated bonded (110) capacitor wafer carries fin-shaped trench plates lined with TiCl4-ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN, its SiN hard mask opened with hot H3PO4.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): crystalline AR >100 from a wet bench costing ~1/20 of a HAR etcher, no fluorinated chemistry; line-shaped plates resist the pillar leaning that limits AR today.

title: Shield-tier interleave makes row hammer geometrically impossible
idea: IFR: 'no wordline has a neighbor to disturb.' Backward: in a 3D horizontal-cell stack, insert a grounded metal shield tier between active tiers and stagger in-plane adjacent rows into alternating tiers, so every row's nearest neighbors are shields or idle tiers; spend cheap extra tiers to buy isolation.
why: Row hammer (fact 9): >10x lower aggressor coupling removes TRR/RFM refresh overhead (~5-10% bandwidth); the price is tiers, the cheap axis in 3D.

title: Vanadium dioxide graded-threshold switches replace the tier staircase
idea: Run one shared vertical select pillar per block through all tiers with a VO2 insulator-metal-transition switch at each tier junction, its thickness graded so switching voltage steps ~0.15 V per tier; ramping this pillar against a counter-pillar opens exactly one tier using two contacts instead of 32.
why: The staircase and per-tier contacts grow in area and mask count with tiers (facts 2, 7); collapsing them into two pillars could save ~5-10% die area and many staircase litho/etch cycles.

title: Micro-row 3D activation: per-tier wordline stubs open 64 bits
idea: Worse: open an 8 KB row for every 64 B request. Flip: in a vertical-wordline 3D array, split each vertical wordline into per-tier stubs behind a local select device at the tier edge, so one activation energizes only one tier of one subarray stripe (64-512 bits).
why: Overfetch falls from 128x to ~1-8x and random-read energy from 5.9 pJ per useful bit to <1 pJ (fact 8); fewer activations also shrink row-hammer exposure (fact 9).

title: Eliminate the landing pad: oxide capacitor grown self-aligned on channel
idea: Delete the storage-node contact and landing-pad litho layer; grow a conductive perovskite oxide (e.g. SrRuO3 or LaNiO3) by selective-area epitaxy only on the exposed top of each vertical channel, so the capacitor bottom electrode self-registers to the transistor with zero overlay margin.
why: Litho-bound scaling: removes one critical (often EUV) layer and its overlay budget, enabling true 4F2 without pad-to-pillar misalignment; ~10-15% cost/bit.

title: Liquid-nitrogen DRAM: shrink capacitors 10x since leakage vanishes
idea: Inverts 'DRAM runs at room temperature.' Operate memory slabs at 77 K in LN2 made from air on site (no helium), where junction and subthreshold leakage collapse, so capacitors can be ~10x smaller (AR ~7:1) and refresh essentially stops.
why: Facts 1 and 3 plus the helium chokepoint: refresh power ~0 and the capacitor wall removed; cryocooler power of ~10x the heat removed is the honest cost.

title: Sense amps built from tier transistors inside each 3D tier
idea: Swap periphery and array roles in an oxide-semiconductor 3D DRAM: build n-only clocked, capacitively bootstrapped sense amplifiers from the same IGZO transistors beside every mat in every tier, so each tier senses locally and only digital data drops to the CMOS base.
why: Periphery (fact 7) and 3D bitline routing (fact 2): removes the vertical analog bitline-to-CMOS bottleneck and keeps bitlines short per tier; ~5-10 ns slower sensing is tolerable.

title: Eliminate on-die redundancy: system-level page retirement replaces spares
idea: Drop spare rows, columns and laser-fuse boxes; ship each die with a signed bad-region map that the memory controller and OS use to retire 4 KB pages, accepting a few tenths of a percent of lost capacity.
why: Cost per bit: recovers ~3-6% die area and removes laser repair and its test step from the back end.

title: Kinematic-coupling self-alignment for cheap fine-pitch die stacking
idea: Use precision-optics kinematic mounts (three balls in three V-grooves): etch inverted pyramids into the base die and tapered posts on each tier die so dies settle into sub-50 nm registration by geometry during fluid-assisted placement, letting fast coarse pick-and-place feed fine-pitch hybrid bonding.
why: Stacking capital and throughput (facts 4, 6): replaces $10M-class high-precision die-to-wafer bonders with fast placement plus self-alignment; claims 5-10x bonding throughput.

title: Block-copolymer gyroid sponge as a giant-area storage capacitor
idea: Po: the capacitor is a sponge. Self-assemble a block copolymer into a gyroid network over each access transistor, convert it to a porous metal scaffold with ~10 nm struts, island it per cell with a shallow trench, then ALD electrode/ZrO2/electrode inside for 20-40x projected area.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): area gain replaces the AR 60-75:1 pillar etch, the hardest step; bottom-up patterning removes one EUV layer.

title: Lost-wax gyroid: block-copolymer network cast into capacitor electrodes
idea: Investment-casting analogy: fill each capacitor hole with a gyroid-forming block copolymer, remove one block to leave a ~10 nm-strut 3D network (the wax pattern), ALD-coat TiN over it, burn out the polymer, then coat dielectric and top plate, giving a bicontinuous sponge electrode inside the same hole.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): 3-5x surface area at equal aspect ratio, so ~5 fF is reachable at AR ~20:1 instead of 60-75:1, relaxing etch and support-lattice steps (fact 4).

title: Anodized aluminum foil grows its own capacitor template
idea: IFR: 'the substrate is the capacitor.' Backward: anodize high-purity aluminum foil into self-ordered porous alumina with 200-500:1 pores at ~50-60 nm pitch, remove the pore-bottom barrier so the remaining aluminum base contacts an ALD TiN plate liner, add high-k and a storage-node fill, and build oxide TFT access transistors on top roll-to-roll.
why: Charge wall and capital (facts 1, 4): capacitor AR >200:1 with no etch tool or lithography on a ~$5/m2 non-chokepoint substrate; cell pitch is ~3x coarser, so multi-level charge must close the density gap.

title: Pyroelectric heat-pulse non-destructive read of stacked ferroelectric tiers
idea: Pyroelectric effect: in a 3D-stacked HZO ferroelectric capacitor array, a nanosecond current pulse in a resistive heater line beside each row warms the cells by a few kelvin. Each cell then emits a pyroelectric current whose sign gives its polarization, so the read never switches the cell and the data is non-volatile with no write-back.
why: Removes the destructive read and write-back (fact 8) and the endurance drain of FeRAM reads; claim read energy cut ~5x, with cycling wear only on writes.

title: Piano keys: staggered-height checkerboard capacitors double each level's pitch
idea: Black keys sit higher than white keys: in a checkerboard, even cells' capacitors start on the landing-pad layer while odd cells' capacitors start one level up on a conductive riser. Each level then holds capacitors at 1.41x the lateral pitch with about 2x the cross-section each.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): ~2x storage cross-section at the same density, or the same Cs in a ~25% smaller cell.

title: Coaxial cell: capacitor shells wrapped around the vertical transistor pillar
idea: TRIZ #7 Nesting: in a 4F2 vertical-channel cell, extend the pillar's lower n+ drain upward as a thin outer electrode shell, coat it with high-k, and fill the inter-pillar space with the common plate, while the upper part of the same pillar carries the gate-all-around wordline. Capacitor and transistor live inside one pillar, so there is no storage-node contact or landing-pad layer.
why: Fact 4: 6F2 -> 4F2 (-33% area) and one fewer critical mask; the full pillar sidewall gives ~3-4 fF at AR ~40.

title: Fluorine-free DRAM flow certification as a U.S. permitting fast lane
idea: Create a U.S. 'fluorine-free memory' track: CHIPS/DoD funding and EPA permitting priority for DRAM lines that use no F-gases or PFAS (built from epi stacks + Cl/Br etch + Mo-chloride + AAO/drawn-glass capacitors), with defense/hyperscaler offtake; the fab skips F-GHG point-of-use abatement and PFAS wastewater treatment.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital: est. 12-24 months faster permitting, a few % lower capex, immunity to PFAS bans/supplier exits and to the fluorspar chokepoint (China ~60%+).

title: Aquarium glass: core dies framed in glass carry HBM channels
idea: An aquarium holds its contents in a glass frame: embed each thinned, TSV-free DRAM core die in a glass frame with laser-drilled, Cu-filled through-glass vias, and stack the frames so the vertical HBM channel wiring runs through the glass around the dies, with short RDL fan-in to edge pads. The base die and the HBM3E/HBM4 interface do not change.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6): core dies shed TSV area and keep-out (~10-15% of die) and become standard thin dies; glass is cheap and not a chokepoint.

title: Optical waveguide wordlines with photoconductive access devices
idea: Po: rows are opened by light. Replace metal wordlines with SiN waveguides over each row and use wide-bandgap photoconductors (ZnO or Ga2O3) as access devices that conduct only under a UV row pulse; transparent oxide tiers let one pulse address a vertical column of tiers.
why: Voltage floor (fact 10): removes wordline CV2 (~30% of activation energy) and 3 V drivers; dark photoconductor leakage can be sub-fA.

title: Capacitor first, transistor later: Smart-Cut silicon over a finished capacitor bed
idea: Invert the build order in time: make the capacitor array in a bulk wafer with unlimited thermal budget, then hydrogen-implant and Smart-Cut (1995) a thin single-crystal silicon layer onto it. Build the access transistors on top, contacting the capacitors through self-aligned plugs.
why: Capacitor and transistor processing stop degrading each other (facts 1, 3): high-temperature anneals for higher-k dielectrics, plus pristine single-crystal, low-leakage transistors.

title: Mirror tier pairs to share bitline layers
idea: Flip every second tier upside down so tiers 2k and 2k+1 face each other and share one bitline/contact layer between them (the 3D NAND mirror trick applied to 3D DRAM). It is done by deposition order alone, with zero added masks.
why: Stack height and 3D cost (fact 2): ~25-30% fewer layers per bit tier means more tiers within the same HAR etch budget.

title: Cable TV frequency multiplexing reads eight tiers on one line
idea: Borrowed from FDM in cable TV: each tier's cell group couples to a shared vertical line through an on-tier LC or ring resonator with a distinct frequency; a multi-tone read pulse interrogates 8 tiers at once and the sense chain separates them by frequency.
why: Cuts vertical bitlines and sense amps per footprint ~8x in 3D stacks (fact 7); signal levels are the open risk.

title: 77 K cryogenic stacks let 3D tiers use sub-femtofarad capacitors
idea: Carrier freeze-out of thermal leakage: liquid-nitrogen-cooled 3D DRAM stacks at 77 K cut access-transistor leakage by about 1e6. Lateral tier capacitors of 0.3-0.5 fF then retain data for seconds or more, so planar thin tiers replace high-AR pillars.
why: Breaks the capacitor wall (fact 1) and the 3D blocker (fact 2), and nearly removes refresh (fact 3); claim 10x lower Cs requirement and >100x refresh reduction for datacenter racks.

title: Magnify wafer use: double-sided cells around a mid-height bitline
idea: Bury the bitline at mid-height in the wafer. An upper vertical transistor and capacitor are built on the front side; after bonding and thinning, a second vertical transistor and capacitor are built on the backside, both hanging from the same bitline. Two storage cells then share each 4F2 footprint, for 2F2 effective.
why: Density and litho: doubles bits per mm2 without a smaller F, so the same EUV layer count buys about 2x the bits.

title: Light-switch air gap: NEMS relay access device in BEOL tiers
idea: A wall switch draws nothing when off because of its air gap; make each 3D cell's access device a laterally actuated ~10 nm-gap TiN/Ru NEMS relay built at BEOL temperatures, whose near-zero off-current lets the capacitor shrink to ~0.3 fF (signal-limited, not retention-limited) and removes refresh.
why: Leakage tail and refresh (fact 3): refresh's ~46 fJ/bit disappears and cell plus local-line charge drops ~10x; claims ~10x lower energy per access if contact endurance holds.

title: One Czochralski boule, fifty tiers: repeated hydrogen-cut exfoliation
idea: Inverts 'each stacked tier consumes a wafer.' Split ~100 nm single-crystal Si films from one donor wafer again and again by hydrogen implant and cleave, re-polishing between cuts, so a single crucible-grown wafer supplies ~50 tiers.
why: Quartz-crucible chokepoint: ~50x less CZ silicon (and Spruce Pine quartz) per tier, using only Si and H.

title: Fluorine vapor XeF2 carves lateral capacitor cavities in poly-Si stacks
idea: Deposit an LPCVD poly-Si/SiO2 multilayer, etch a vertical slit, and expose it to XeF2 vapor, which isotropically recesses only the poly-Si (>1000:1 to SiO2) by a timed 100-200 nm; ALD then lines the horizontal cavities with TiN/ZrO2/TiN as lateral capacitors for 8-16 tiers.
why: Demonstrates lateral 3D-DRAM capacitor formation (fact 2) with a plasma-free, stiction-free etch present in most university MEMS labs, avoiding SiGe epi entirely.

title: Eliminate cells: vertical charge-coupled shift-register strings
idea: Delete the per-bit capacitor, transistor and staircase: each vertical hole through 128 tiers is a CCD whose tier gates are tied to only 3 clock phases, so charge packets shift up to a single sense node at the top (128 ns worst-case serial access, pipelined bursts).
why: Water: one hole etch plus one channel deposition serves 128 bits with no capacitor module or tier contacts, so wet cleans and CMP per bit drop by >10x; also removes capacitor charge-wall limits.

title: Block-copolymer self-assembly in 248-nm guides: 12-nm features from a hotplate
idea: Use the molecular scale as the lithographer: coat a PS-b-PMMA block copolymer into 180-nm KrF-printed guide trenches and anneal it. It phase-separates into lamellae or cylinders at 12-25 nm pitch, multiplying the guide frequency 8-15x for bitline or hole patterns using only a spin coater, oven and RIE.
why: EUV dependence (fact 4): sub-20-nm features without EUV or immersion.

title: Well-digger farmer lets chemistry dig: metal-assisted wet etch capacitor holes
idea: The farmer digs wells with water, not drills. Put a patterned Au/Pt catalyst mesh on silicon and immerse it in HF/H2O2: the silicon under the metal dissolves straight down, giving 100-200:1 smooth holes at room temperature in a beaker. ALD then lines them into trench capacitors.
why: Reaches Fact 1's AR ~115 without $50M high-AR plasma etchers, and a 10-person team can run it on a wet bench.

title: Display-fab DRAM: oxide memory tiles on Gen-8.5 glass panels
idea: Under 400 C, display IGZO lines (all at or below 350 C) pattern stacked oxide 1T1C arrays on 2.2x2.5 m glass at about 1.5 um rules, using thick-film capacitors. Panels are diced into memory tiles that are bonded under logic as capacity tiers.
why: Capital intensity and cost per bit: about 25x the area of a 300 mm wafer per substrate, on depreciated tools; good for bulk capacity tiers.

title: Shingled mushroom capacitors: SMR-style overlap of two height tiers
idea: Like shingled magnetic recording overlapping tracks, build capacitors in two interleaved heights: even cells get a short pillar topped by a wide mushroom electrode at level 1, odd cells a taller pillar whose cap sits at level 2, so every cap overhangs its neighbours' footprint.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): ~1.8x electrode area per footprint at unchanged aspect ratio, giving either ~9 fF or a cell shrink at constant Cs.

title: Vertical CCD charge-shift strings as append-only KV-cache memory
idea: An AI KV-cache is written once in order and read back as a stream, so build a 3D-NAND-like vertical string but run it as a charge-coupled device: 128 stacked gate tiers around one channel pass charge packets along the string by 3-phase clocking to a single sense node at the top. There is no per-cell access transistor, capacitor or contact; a bit is just one gate crossing.
why: Density ~30-50x bits per mm2 vs planar 6F2, no capacitor (fact 1), periphery amortized over 128 bits per string (fact 7), and no per-bit bitline swing (fact 8); latency is sequential, which suits KV traffic.

title: Eliminate pitch-defining lithography: rotated superlattice slices
idea: Grow a 1000-period Si/SiGe or Si/oxide multilayer whose film thicknesses set the 10-12 nm line pitch, slice it perpendicular to the layers, and bond the slab flat so the layers become parallel bitlines/channels; litho is needed only for coarse cuts.
why: Litho and capital: replaces 5-7 EUV layers with epitaxy thickness control (Angstrom precision), attacking the ~55% depreciation share of wafer cost.

title: Vertical BiSb spin-Hall pillar writes MTJs on eight tiers
idea: Spin Hall effect: a vertical bismuth-antimony topological-insulator pillar (no tungsten) threads eight BEOL tiers of perpendicular MTJs. Current in the pillar delivers spin-orbit torque to every MTJ along it, and a voltage-controlled-anisotropy bias on one tier's MTJ chooses which bit actually switches.
why: Gives non-volatile 3D SOT density with one write line per column (fact 2) and avoids the W chokepoint; claim 8x bits per footprint versus planar SOT-MRAM.

title: Magnify yield: stitch rejected DRAM dies into good ones
idea: Buy partially failing or downbinned DRAM dies at scrap prices, then pair three partial dies under a small remap and sparing logic die (FPGA first, then a $100k MPW ASIC) that presents one fully good logical die in a stacked package.
why: Scarce supply: turns DRAM yield fallout (a few % of output) into sellable capacity at about 30-50% of contract price, with no fab.

title: Seeded cast-mono tiers: single-crystal upper layers by rapid melt growth
idea: Solar cast-mono ingots grow single-crystal silicon from seed plates; do the same per tier by depositing amorphous Si/SiGe in oxide crucibles with a seed via to crystalline silicon below, flash-melting for microseconds and letting it recrystallize laterally into single-crystal islands for lateral access transistors.
why: Gives monolithic 3D tiers crystalline channels with a tight leakage tail (fact 3) without strain-limited Si/SiGe superlattice stacks (fact 2); microsecond flash keeps lower tiers below damage temperature.

title: Silicon-carbide EV fabs make hot, near-refresh-free trench DRAM
idea: IFR: 'memory never refreshes and runs at 125 C.' Backward: use the 150/200 mm 4H-SiC lines overbuilt for EV inverters to make trench-capacitor 1T1C arrays whose 3.3 eV bandgap gives leakage orders below silicon (hours of retention at 125 C), sold as hot-side memory next to accelerators.
why: Refresh (fact 3) and U.S. manufacturability: refresh energy and bandwidth loss near zero; U.S. SiC capacity (NC, NY) is under-loaded, though first-generation density is ~20-50x below DRAM.

title: Vertical tier-column pages replace 8 kb horizontal rows
idea: Substitute the horizontal row as the unit of activation with a vertical slice: one activation opens N tiers x a 16-bitline group (e.g., 32x16 = 512 bits, one 64 B line); tier-select lines act as the row address and the vertical bitline pillar group is the page, each pillar landing on its own sense amp in a bonded CMOS wafer.
why: Destructive read and 128x overfetch (fact 8): 8 kb -> 512 b page cuts activation energy ~10x toward ~0.6 pJ per useful bit; activations spread over many small pages dilute hammer counts.

title: Sol-gel gallium oxide printed channels give day-scale retention
idea: Inkjet or slot-die print Ga2O3 sol-gel channels (Eg ~4.8 eV), densify them by deep-UV photo-annealing below 250 C, and use them as access transistors in foil arrays with 4k-cell bitlines, since refresh traffic disappears.
why: Leakage scales as exp(-Eg/2kT), so at 4.8 eV intrinsic generation is negligible; with defect-limited off-current ~1e-21 A an 8 fF cell loses 10% only after ~days, removing refresh energy and bandwidth (fact 3) and going beyond the IGZO already studied.

title: Two-out-of-five constant-weight codes enable reference-free ranked sensing
idea: Revive the IBM 650 / Bell relay 2-out-of-5 code: each group of n cells is written as a constant-weight word and sensed by picking the k strongest cells with a winner-take-all comparator instead of a fixed reference, so tier-to-tier Vt shifts and common leakage cancel. Residual ~1% rank flips are fixed by an outer code.
why: Facts 2 and 3: no dummy/reference bitlines and ~4x longer retention because drift becomes common-mode; tolerates poorly matched 3D tiers.

title: Antiferroelectric gate held between its double loops as volatile bistable
idea: TRIZ #36 Phase transition: use a ZrO2 antiferroelectric layer in each cell transistor's gate and park the wordline plane at a hold bias between the two hysteresis loops, where both the nonpolar and the field-induced polar phase are stable. A short over- or under-pulse toggles the phase and the channel Vt reads it.
why: Fact 1 and 3: capacitorless 1T cell, minor-loop AFE switching aims at >10^12 cycles, no refresh while the hold bias is on, and whole 3D tiers share one gate plane.

title: Ferreed-like latching NEMS relays as access devices in 3D tiers
idea: Revive the Bell ferreed crosspoint (a reed latched by remanent magnetism) as each 3D cell's access device: a ruthenium-contact nanoelectromechanical relay with essentially zero off-current, built in BEOL tiers without single-crystal silicon or tungsten. With leakage gone, storage capacitors shrink to ~1-2 fF, sized only for read margin on short local bitlines.
why: Facts 1, 2 and 3: lifts the capacitor charge wall (AR from ~70:1 toward ~20:1), nearly eliminates refresh, and avoids China-dominated tungsten.

title: Toshiba chain FeRAM stood vertically as 3D ferroelectric strings
idea: Revive Toshiba's 1997 chain FeRAM, where each cell's transistor shunts its own ferroelectric capacitor in a series chain: build it as a vertical string of 32 shunted capacitors per pillar, 3D-NAND style, and accept ~1% read-disturb flips in neighbours that a per-string code corrects on write-back.
why: Facts 2 and 4: a 3D ferroelectric cell with one channel hole per 32 bits; error tolerance lets mismatched shunt devices and thin HZO work.

title: Two-nanometer silicon channels widen the bandgap to starve leakage
idea: Thin the access channel to ~2 nm by oxidation-trimming epitaxial nanosheets so quantum confinement raises the effective bandgap by ~0.3-0.5 eV; drive current remains adequate because each cell holds little charge.
why: Leakage physics: generation and band-to-band leakage scale roughly as exp(-Eg/2kT), so +0.4 eV gives ~3 decades less tail leakage (fact 3), moving silicon refresh from 64 ms toward ~1 min without exotic oxides.

title: EHD jet-printed pillar capacitors grown upward, never etched
idea: Use multi-nozzle electrohydrodynamic jet printing to stack silver nanoparticle droplets into 0.5 um-wide, 5 um-tall pillars on each cell's storage pad, then coat them with spatial-ALD AlOx and a conformal printed counter-electrode.
why: Additive growth escapes the aspect-ratio-dependent etch limit behind the charge wall (fact 1): C=eA/d over a 0.5x5 um pillar with 8 nm AlOx is ~80 fF, ~15x today's Cs, allowing ~10x longer bitlines and far fewer sense amps per foil.

title: Skyscraper sky lobbies: tier-local sense amps every 16 tiers
idea: Adapted from supertall-building sky lobbies (express elevator to a lobby, local elevators onward): long vertical bitlines in a 3D DRAM stack are cut into 16-tier segments, each ending at a 'sky lobby' tier holding oxide-TFT local sense amps that drive a low-swing express global bitline down to CMOS.
why: Bitline capacitance seen per sense drops ~8x, so Cs can shrink from ~5 fF to <1 fF with the same margin (fact 1) and stacks can exceed 100 tiers without a high-AR capacitor (fact 2).

title: Grounded shield-plate tiers that make row hammer impossible
idea: Limit: no row may have an electrically coupled neighbor. Insert a thin grounded metal plane between every pair of cell tiers, and alternate wordline tiers between different banks. The plane blocks both capacitive crosstalk and carrier migration from aggressor rows.
why: Fact 9: pushes the flip threshold from about 1k activations to far beyond any refresh window and removes mitigation logic and its bandwidth cost.

title: Precast concrete: test each crystalline tier before stacking it
idea: Like precast panels cured and inspected off-site, each single-crystal DRAM tier is built on a donor, wafer-tested, and only then transferred by hydrogen smart-cut onto the stack, with bad sub-arrays remapped before the next tier is added.
why: Monocrystalline lateral transistors in every tier (facts 2,3: tighter leakage tail) and stack yield that does not compound per tier, making 26+ tiers economic.

title: Minify refresh by die position: per-die refresh in HBM stacks
idea: On an FPGA-with-HBM board, measure how retention varies with each die's position in the stack, then have a custom controller issue per-channel refresh at rates matched to each die's measured temperature and retention rather than the hottest die.
why: Refresh in 3D stacks: could cut refresh by about 30-40% on cooler dies, using firmware and controller IP that cost about $300k.

title: Gleaner's leftover grain: restacking fab-rejected DRAM dies
idea: Gleaners collect the grain harvesters leave behind. A 10-person team buys binned-out DRAM dies (partial-bank fails, weak retention, slow bins) at scrap prices, thins them, and stacks 8 on a small base ASIC that maps out dead banks and sets per-die refresh. The stacks are sold as capacity modules for AI KV caches.
why: Turns ~5-10% of scrapped fab output into usable supply with no new wafers. Capex is a die bonder and a wire bonder.

title: Interdigitating nano-comb bond splits one capacitor across two wafers
idea: Substitute one AR-115 capacitor etch with two AR-40 etches: wafer A carries storage-node pillars, wafer B carries matching holes lined with ZrO2 and the plate electrode; face-to-face hybrid bonding with ~10 nm overlay slides pillars into holes, producing a capacitor whose electrode length is the sum of both.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): Cs ~5->9 fF with no etch above 40:1, each etch cheaper and higher-yield; plate wafer moves off the critical path.

title: Zero-stray-field Mn3Sn antiferromagnetic bits packed at sub-ferromagnetic pitch
idea: Anomalous Hall effect in noncollinear antiferromagnets: Mn3Sn bits switched by spin-orbit torque are read by their large anomalous Hall or tunneling signal. Because antiferromagnets emit no dipolar stray field, neighboring bits and stacked tiers can be packed far tighter than ferromagnetic MTJs without crosstalk.
why: Gives denser non-volatile 3D packing with ps-scale switching (facts 2 and 5); claim ~2x tighter pitch per tier than ferromagnetic MRAM and field-immune bits.

title: Tree-ring staircase: CMP a trench-filled stack to expose every tier
idea: Like grinding Damascus steel or turning a log to reveal growth rings, deposit the tier stack conformally into a wide sloped trench and CMP flat, so every tier surfaces as its own band and wordline contacts land with one lithography step instead of 10-30 resist-trim and etch cycles.
why: Staircase formation costs area and many litho/etch loops as tiers grow (facts 2, 4); one CMP plus one contact mask could cut staircase cost >5x and area ~2x.

title: Argon fast-atom activated Si-Si bonding replaces HF-last tier bonding
idea: Substitute HF-dip hydrophobic bonding and oxide-interface bonding with room-temperature surface-activated bonding: an Ar fast-atom beam in UHV strips the native oxide and two single-crystal Si tiers are pressed into a conductive, oxide-free junction, so vertical bitline/channel pillars run continuously through layer-transferred tiers.
why: Monolithic-quality 3D tiers (fact 2) with dry, fluorine-free surface prep; conductive bonds remove one via per tier per pillar (~10-20% fewer steps per tier).

title: Thermophile compact core: 2 nm silicon sheets raise bandgap, shrink leak volume
idea: Hyperthermophile proteins keep compact cores with few exposed loops; make the 3D lateral access transistor a quantum-confined 2-3 nm epitaxial Si nanosheet, which raises the effective bandgap to ~1.5 eV and cuts the depleted generation volume ~20x versus a bulk junction, with a metal storage node silicided directly to the sheet.
why: At 125 C SRH generation in depletion regions dominates leakage; wider effective gap plus tiny volume could cut the 125 C leakage tail ~50-100x and keep 64 ms refresh at grade-1 temperature.

title: Corrugated cardboard: rippled capacitor walls boost electrode area
idea: Corrugation adds surface: during the lateral-capacitor recess in a 3D stack, or the pillar etch in 2D, alternate etch and passivation cycles (Bosch-like scalloping) or a Si/SiGe sub-superlattice with selective recess give the electrode rippled walls before conformal ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN. The cell footprint and the DDR5/HBM interface do not change.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): electrode area 1.5-2x, so Cs 7-9 fF at today's aspect ratio or today's Cs at AR ~40:1.

title: ISO-container memory tile: an open hybrid-bond array standard
idea: Standardize a memory container: a 1 Gb array tile with fixed footprint, fixed hybrid-bond pad map (sense-amp interface, power, test) and fixed timing protocol, so any maker's array tile bonds onto any vendor's base die, as ISO containers did for shipping.
why: Capital intensity and supply diversity (facts 4, 6): new array makers (oxide, 3D, legacy fabs) can enter without building periphery and I/O; claims faster capacity ramp and commodity tile pricing.

title: Pixel-detector bonding: every 16 bitlines get their own sense-amp bond
idea: Particle-physics pixel detectors bond each sensor pixel to its own readout channel; hybrid-bond the DRAM array wafer at ~0.4 um pitch so every group of 16 bitlines, muxed by an in-array selector, lands on its own sense amplifier on a separately made logic wafer. The array wafer then holds no sense amps, decoders or I/O at all.
why: Periphery ~49% of the die (fact 7) moves to a cheap logic wafer: ~2x array-wafer area per bit, and logic-process sense amps run faster at lower voltage (fact 10).

title: Corrugated substrate hosts planar arrays on both sidewall faces
idea: Po: the wafer is not flat. Etch the silicon into 20:1 parallel walls before front-end processing, then build planar-transistor DRAM conformally on both wall faces with tilted implants and conformal ALD gates, so 1 cm2 of footprint carries ~10-20 cm2 of active surface.
why: Density without tier deposition: ~10x surface at relaxed F with no EUV; capacitors can run long along the wall.

title: Vinyl-record pressing: nanoimprint stampers for capacitor and channel layers
idea: Records are pressed from nickel stampers replicated from one master; write one e-beam master of the capacitor-hole layer, electroform daughter stampers, and imprint every wafer in mature fabs, aligning to coarse periphery marks.
why: Swaps EUV exposures (fact 4) for imprint at a fraction of tool cost; imprint defects are tolerable in regular arrays with row redundancy.

title: Public golden DRAM array mask set, one private mask
idea: Policy: fund an open, government-owned reference DRAM array mask set and process (the cell, capacitor and bitline layers) that any U.S. fab or startup can license, each differentiating with one private periphery or personalization mask, reversing DRAM from closed IP to shared infrastructure.
why: Capital and U.S. manufacturability (fact 4): removes the multi-year array development barrier for new entrants; mask NRE is shared across all fabs.

title: Bonded bit-planes sharing one base-die row decoder, core-stack style
idea: Treat each hybrid-bonded DRAM array die like a core-memory bit plane: dies are thinned to ~5 um and carry sub-micron through-die vias at mat edges so one row decoder/driver on the base logic die drives the same wordline in all 16 planes, while each plane delivers one bit slice of the word. Array dies keep only cells and sense amps.
why: Facts 6 and 7: deletes row decoders and charge pumps from 15 of 16 dies (~15-20% of each die), giving ~15-25% lower cost per bit for stacked DRAM.

title: Two-deck capacitor molds joined like 3D NAND channel decks
idea: [Box: MIM | VCT | charge-share SA | monolithic | Si | two sequential 50:1 mold decks + self-aligned conductive inter-deck plug] Etch the capacitor mold as two stacked 50:1 decks joined by a self-aligned plug, building electrodes in each, for ~100:1 effective height from ArF-resolvable holes and production-proven etches.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): ~100-115 effective AR without new etch physics or EUV.

title: Williams-tube margin raster: scrub weak charges, stretch refresh 16x
idea: Williams tubes kept their spots alive by continuous raster regeneration; revive it as a base-die scrub engine that sweeps 3D tiers with a three-level sense (strong-1, weak-1, 0), rewrites only weak cells, and lets the refresh interval stretch until ~1% of cells have leaked, which the code then corrects.
why: Fact 3: refresh energy and bandwidth loss fall ~10x (64 ms toward ~1 s) by tolerating the leakage tail instead of designing for it.

title: Area-selective ALD grows landing pads only on contacts
idea: [Box: MIM | VCT | standard SA | monolithic | Si | inhibitor-based area-selective ALD of Ru on TiN, not on SiO2] Replace the overlay-critical landing-pad and storage-contact lithography with bottom-up growth: inhibitor molecules passivate the dielectric, and Ru nucleates only on exposed contacts, self-limiting into mushroom pads.
why: No EUV (fact 4): removes 1-2 critical layers and their overlay budget, because each pad is self-aligned to its contact.

title: Space cold-welding: atomic-hydrogen activated room-temperature Cu-Cu bonding
idea: In orbit, clean metals cold-weld on contact; reproduce this by reducing copper and SiCN bond surfaces with atomic hydrogen from a hot-filament H2 cracker in vacuum, instead of argon fast-atom beams or argon plasma, then pressing die to wafer at room temperature. No anneal is needed, so bonded DRAM tiers never see the 350-400 C that degrades retention.
why: Room-temperature bonding protects the leakage tail (fact 3), allows sub-0.5 um pitch with no copper expansion, and supports more bonded tiers (facts 2 and 6) without argon.

title: Epitaxial thyristor cross-point decks: no capacitor, no access transistor
idea: Worse: build a capacitor plus a transistor for every bit. Flip: grow p-n-p-n layers and self-align-etch them into cross-point pillars between orthogonal word and bit lines so each crossing is a gated bistable thyristor cell, and stack 12 decks where every line layer serves the deck above and below.
why: 4F2 per deck at F=16 nm (DUV SAQP) across 12 decks is ~85 nm2/bit (~10x), patterned with ~13 DUV line masks, roughly the cost of the 4-5 EUV layers it replaces (fact 4).

title: Carbon-nanotube CMOS periphery on glass beneath oxide arrays
idea: IFR: 'periphery is fast, complementary and made at 200 C.' Backward: deposit aligned >99.99% semiconducting carbon-nanotube films on glass, build n- and p-type CNFET sense amps and decoders at <=250 C, then stack oxide-semiconductor cell tiers directly above with no thermal damage.
why: Periphery (fact 7) and 3D: complementary periphery-under-array with no silicon wafer, enabling unlimited monolithic tiers above; ~3-10x lower logic energy than oxide-only periphery.

title: BCB polymer bonding repurposed as debond-on-demand tier interlayer
idea: BCB adhesive wafer bonding was abandoned for 3D stacking because it degrades above ~350C. Make that a feature: bond DRAM tiers with a thin, thermally decomposable polymer pierced by short copper nails for signals. At end of life a bake separates the tiers for retest and reuse, or for clean copper and silicon recovery.
why: Makes multi-tier stacks (facts 2, 6) recyclable into reusable dies or clean material streams instead of mixed shredder waste.

title: Vertical charge-coupled strings: bits march through 128 gate tiers
idea: Worse: give every bit its own access transistor, capacitor and contact. Flip: store bits as charge packets in a vertical CCD channel threaded through a 128-tier stack of 3-phase clocked gate plates, shifting them to one sense/regenerate node at the base, which also refreshes each packet as it recirculates.
why: A bit costs ~3 gate tiers in one hole with no capacitor or per-bit transistor: ~42 bits per 60 nm-pitch hole ~74 nm2/bit versus 864 nm2 for 6F2 at F=12 nm (~11x) with a 3D-NAND-like flow at similar wafer cost; refresh is built in, and 32-stage segments keep latency in the 10-100 ns range.

title: Oil-well drilling: revive U.S. deep-trench eDRAM modules as DRAM bricks
idea: Deep-trench capacitors are drilled into the substrate like oil wells; restart deep-trench eDRAM process modules in U.S. SOI trailing fabs to make stand-alone eDRAM brick chiplets with trench Cs above 10 fF for L4 and near-memory caches.
why: Proven 1T1C trench cells with long retention at 22-32 nm, no EUV, U.S.-made; displaces part of HBM demand for cache-like working sets.

title: Magnify usable bits: reclaim on-die ECC parity cells
idea: DDR5 dies carry about 6.25% extra cells for on-die ECC. Partner with a second-tier vendor to expose a test-mode map that releases those cells as user capacity for error-tolerant data such as AI weights and caches, with protection handled by host-side ECC.
why: Supply: about 6% more usable bits from every die already built. Only firmware, characterization and a vendor deal are needed, about $500k.

title: Basement-and-rooftop sandwich: periphery split across two bonded wafers
idea: Copy buildings that put plant rooms in the basement and on the roof: a three-wafer stack with row decoders and wordline drivers bonded below the array wafer and sense amplifiers plus column logic bonded above it, each at line pitch, leaving the middle array wafer 100% cells.
why: Periphery ~49% of die (fact 7): array efficiency rises toward ~90%; claims ~1.7x bits per array-wafer area with periphery on cheaper logic nodes.

title: Junctionless transferred-silicon tiers from pre-doped donor wafers
idea: Under 400 C, H/He co-implant splits a heavily pre-doped donor at 350 C after a 250 C plasma-activated bond. The 10 nm single-crystal film becomes junctionless access transistors that never need a dopant-activation anneal.
why: Fact 2: crystalline-Si mobility and controlled leakage in 3D tiers without the 1000 C steps that stop monolithic stacking.

title: Column-inversion storage cancels bitline coupling, like LCD panels
idea: LCD drivers alternate pixel polarity column by column to cancel crosstalk; store data in alternating true/complement polarity on adjacent bitlines and flip the pattern each row, so neighbour-swing coupling arrives common-mode at each sense amp and cancels, allowing tighter vertical-bitline pitch without shield lines.
why: Density in 3D arrays and signal margin (facts 1, 2): removes shield lines (~20-30% of bitline pitch) and recovers ~30% signal; claims ~1.25x density.

title: Double helix: vertical bitline pairs twist between tiers, cancelling noise
idea: Like DNA strands swapping sides, true and complement vertical bitlines in a 3D array swap positions every 8 tiers through crossover vias, so coupling from neighbor bitlines and wordline steps lands equally on both and cancels in the sense amp. Vertical bitlines can then pack at minimum spacing without shields, inside a standard DDR5/HBM die.
why: 3D blocker (fact 2) and capacitor wall (fact 1): bitline coupling noise ~5x lower, allowing smaller sense signals (lower Cs) and ~20% tighter vertical bitline pitch.

title: Tesla-valve diode cells: crosspoint 1D1C array without wordline gates
idea: A Tesla valve rectifies flow with no moving parts; build a crosspoint 3D array where each capacitor is reached through a wide-bandgap Ga2O3/NiO heterojunction thin-film diode, selected by coincidence of a 1.2 V row-plate pulse and a bitline offset, removing the 3 V gated wordline and the access transistor.
why: Voltage floor and density (facts 2, 10): no VPP wordline and 4F2 crosspoint stacking in BEOL; claims ~10x lower select energy, provided diode reverse leakage stays below ~1 fA.

title: LC-resonant paired wordlines recycle charge between adjacent rows
idea: Electrical resonance: adjacent wordlines are paired through a spiral inductor in the bonding layer, so falling-row charge resonantly transfers to the rising row (adiabatic energy recovery) instead of being dumped to ground at each activate.
why: Attacks the stuck CV2 energy of ~3 V wordlines (fact 10); claim 50-70% wordline energy recovery and smaller charge pumps (fact 7).
